title: Constructive Root Bounds from Descartes Rule of Signs

problemStatement.formal: axiom descartes_upper_bound_axiom (p : ℝ[X]) (hp : p ≠ 0) : countPositiveRoots p ≤ signChangesInCoeffs p
problemStatement.plain: Descartes' Rule of Signs: the number of positive real roots of a polynomial (counted with multiplicity) is at most equal to the number of sign changes in its coefficient sequence, and the difference is even.
whyMatters: Fundamental theorem connecting coefficient patterns to root structure
One of the first systematic methods for root analysis (1637)

proven: Sign change counting framework (realSign, oppositeSign, SignChangeBetween)
Descartes' Rule combined: upper bound + parity = exact characterization
Negative root variant via p(-x) substitution
negSubst preserves non-zero polynomials (proved via double composition)
Constant polynomials have no positive roots
X^n has no positive roots (0 is not positive)
Non-negative coefficients imply no positive roots
Rolle's theorem connection for derivative roots
